newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia SBI sheds 8 pct, erases five-day gains.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia SBI sheds 8 pct, erases five-day gains.

text.p: Slovenia's SBI index reversed a spectacular five-day winning streak on Tuesday, shedding over eight percent as investors took fright from the central bank's clampdown on foreign trading activity, traders said.
The blue-chip SBI ended 140.59 points, or 8.46 percent, lower at 1,521.83 -- more than wiping out the gains from the fledgling bourse's most recent bull run.
The central bank said on Tuesday that foreign investors in Slovenian shares must in future hold special trading accounts with fully licensed banks if they wanted to invest in domestic companies.
"In this way we wanted to organise foreign portfolio investment in Slovenia," Darko Bohnec, head of central bank operations, told Reuters.
Market participants were taken aback by the move.
"This is a shock to the market. The procedure on how these accounts have to be established is not clear," said Aleksander Simon, an analyst at Nova Ljubljanska Banka.
"Shares may continue falling until things become clearer," he added.
Buying from foreign investors had helped drive the Slovenian market up 40 percent since the beginning of the year.
On Monday, the index hit an all-time high of 1,662.42 but traders held out little hope for the market recapturing that level any time soon.

"I see the index falling 30 to 50 percent from yesterday's levels if the Bank of Slovenia does not change its position -- which is not going to happen very soon," Goran Brankovic, a trader at Nova Ljubljanskla Banka said.
Trading company Kovinotehna was the day's leading decliner, shedding 12.76 percent to 506 tolars on volume of 12,887 tolars.
Overall 14 shares fell, two rose, one was unchanged, while another eight were untraded.
